titel: Interest rate risk and stress test
kurz: What risk lies in the outstanding balance after a ten-year fixed-rate period, what a follow-up interest rate two points higher costs and how this can be calculated before signing.

bloecke.md:
A ten-year fixed-rate period secures the interest rate, but not the terms for the outstanding balance afterwards. Anyone financing in 2026 knows their instalment to the cent until 2036, but nothing about the instalment after that. This uncertainty is [[Interest rate risk|interest rate risk]]. With standard German mortgage financing it is large, because the initial repayment rate is traditionally set low.

In the base case of this lesson, the purchase price is €460,000, the incidental purchase costs around €46,000, the equity €106,000 and the loan €400,000. With monthly payments, a borrowing rate of 3.90% results in an effective interest rate of 3.97%. This corresponds to the offer rate for ten-year fixed-rate periods published by the mortgage broker Dr. Klein on 3 September 2026. The initial repayment rate is 2%, so the annuity is 5.9% of €400,000, which is €23,600 a year or €1,966.67 a month. Net household income is €5,200, the living space 120 square metres, and the building dates from 2019.

After ten years, this household has transferred €236,000 to the bank, of which €138,300 is interest and €97,700 repayment. That leaves €302,300 outstanding, just over three quarters of the original debt. This amount has to be refinanced when the fixed-rate period ends.

bloecke.erklaerung: The formula calculates the outstanding balance after k months. It therefore gives the amount that has to be refinanced at an interest rate that is unknown today, and it is the basis of the entire stress test.
variablen: monthly interest rate, that is, the borrowing rate divided by twelve

bloecke.titel: Effect of the initial repayment rate in the stress case (€400,000, 3.90% borrowing rate, 10-year fixed-rate period)

bloecke.md:
## Initial repayment rate as protection

The far right-hand column assumes that the monthly instalment remains unchanged from year 11 and that the term is extended accordingly. A two-point rise in interest rates then costs the household with a 2% initial repayment rate just over six additional years of debt service, and the household with 4% only eight months. The difference lies in the outstanding balance to which the new interest rate is applied. It is €302,300 with a 2% and €204,700 with a 4% initial repayment rate.

The effect diminishes with each additional percentage point. The step from 2% to 3% repayment costs €333 more a month and shortens the term in the stress case by almost eleven years. The step from 3% to 4% also costs €333 and brings only five years. Additional money for the instalment therefore has the strongest effect when it raises the initial repayment rate from 2% to 3%.

Affordability is decided by the outstanding balance at the end of the fixed-rate period, not by the instalment of the first ten years. The outstanding balance is the only variable in the financing that is fixed today and only takes effect in ten years.

bloecke.md:
## Debt service capacity and housing cost ratio

Banks check [[Debt service capacity|debt service capacity]]. Net income, less a flat-rate amount for living costs and existing obligations, must cover the annuity. This creditworthiness assessment has been mandatory since the Mortgage Credit Directive (Section 505a BGB, Civil Code). If the bank breaches it, Section 505d BGB reduces the borrowing rate to the usual market rate and gives the borrower a right to terminate at any time without an early repayment charge.

For your own decision, the [[Housing cost ratio|housing cost ratio]] is more suitable. It divides the sum of the annuity and running costs by net household income. In the base case, that is an instalment of €1,967, a maintenance reserve of €115 and €150 for property tax (Grundsteuer) and residential buildings insurance. The reserve is based on 120 square metres at €11.50 per square metre per year under Section 28 II. BV (Second Computation Ordinance) at the level applicable since 2026, age category under 22 years. Together, that is €2,232 or 43% of €5,200. The burden is therefore already high before an interest rate rise or a loss of income comes on top.

bloecke.titel: Housing cost ratio in year 11, as a percentage of net household income
bloecke.unter: Illustrative calculation with the instalment at the follow-up interest rate for the same remaining term plus €265 in running costs, based on three income paths over ten years.

bloecke.md: A follow-up calculation with today's income overstates the burden, because nominal incomes have usually risen after ten years. A calculation with extrapolated income understates it, because the instalment is fixed by contract, whereas income growth is not fixed anywhere. Parental leave, part-time work, an industry crisis or illness can make your own income deviate from the development of the economy as a whole, which it only follows on average. You should therefore calculate both variants and decide on the basis of the less favourable result.

A stress test that only changes the interest rate is incomplete. A rise in interest rates affects the instalment, and only in ten years' time. The other scenarios affect income and can occur at any time.

bloecke.md:
## Unemployment

Unemployment benefit I (Arbeitslosengeld I) amounts to 60% of flat-rate net pay, or 67% with at least one child (Section 149 SGB III). “Flat-rate” means that a social security flat rate of 20%, wage tax (Lohnsteuer) and the solidarity surcharge are deducted from the gross pay of the last twelve months. The result is usually below the net pay shown on the payslip.

In the base case, earner A brings in €3,000 net and earner B €2,200. If A becomes unemployed, unemployment benefit is roughly €1,800 and household income around €4,000. The housing cost ratio then rises from 43% to 56%. With a reserve, this can be sustained for twelve months; without one, it cannot.

Unemployment benefit is followed by basic income support (Grundsicherungsgeld, until June 2026 Bürgergeld), which only partly covers the costs of an owner-occupied home. The owner-occupied home of appropriate size remains protected as an asset (Section 12 SGB II, Social Code Book II: as a standard, 140 square metres for a house or 130 square metres for a flat for up to four people). As accommodation needs under Section 22 SGB II, however, only the interest on the debt is covered, not the repayment, because repayment counts as wealth accumulation. In a crisis, the part of the instalment that reduces the debt is therefore not reimbursed.

## Separation

Legally, separation is the most complicated case, because the land register, the loan agreement and the internal relationship between the partners diverge. Both partners are liable to the bank as joint and several debtors (Section 421 BGB). [[Joint and several liability]] means that the bank can demand the full instalment from either of them, regardless of who moves out and what the partners have agreed between themselves. The internal settlement between the partners under Section 426 BGB only comes afterwards and is irrelevant to the bank.

A release from liability amounts to a new loan agreement. It requires the remaining partner to carry the financing alone, and with an instalment of €1,967 and €3,000 net income, that is not possible. If the co-owners cannot agree, what remains is a partition auction under Section 180 ZVG, which regularly ends below the price of a private sale. The partners can get out of the loan itself. Section 490(2) BGB grants a right of termination with three months' notice if there is a legitimate interest in otherwise realising the property. The bank can then demand an early repayment charge.

bloecke.titel: Early repayment charges in the 2026 interest rate environment
bloecke.md:
The cap of 1% or 0.5% of the amount repaid in Section 502(3) BGB applies only to general consumer loans, not to mortgage loans. With mortgage loans, the bank is compensated for its actual interest loss, that is, the difference between the agreed interest rate and what the bank can still earn today with the money flowing back.

If the interest rate level rises, this loss becomes smaller. A contract concluded in 2021 at just over 1% costs hardly anything if it is paid off in 2026. For contracts concluded today, the opposite applies. If interest rates fall significantly by 2030, early exit becomes expensive. The amount of the [[Early repayment charge|early repayment charge]] therefore depends on how interest rates have developed since the contract was concluded.

## Affordable financing and rules of thumb

According to a widespread rule, the instalment should not exceed 35% of net household income. This rule has no sound derivation and two systematic flaws.

First, it scales incorrectly. Of €3,000 net, €1,950 remains for all other expenses after a 35% instalment; of €10,000 net, €6,500 remains. But the second household does not need three times as much to live on. Percentage rules are therefore too generous for low incomes and too strict for high ones.

Second, the result depends entirely on the interest rate level, although the rule does not take it into account. With a 2% initial repayment rate and a 1.0% borrowing rate, a monthly instalment of €1,800 supports a loan of €720,000; at 3.90%, only €366,000. Between the zero interest rate period and 2026, the purchasing power of the same household has thus roughly halved, without anything having changed in its situation. However, the comparison only applies to a limited extent. At 1.0% interest and 2% repayment, the loan runs for over 40 years, which is why a significantly higher initial repayment rate was recommended at the time.

Only the residual income calculation is useful. It deducts the measured expenses from net income and determines the affordable instalment from what is left, instead of applying a flat percentage.

schritte.text: The basis is three months of account statements, plus the annual items divided by twelve. Estimated living costs almost always turn out too low.
These include maintenance under Section 28 II. BV, property tax and residential buildings insurance and, for flats, also the non-recoverable service charge (Hausgeld).

schritte.titel: Deduct retirement provision before the instalment
schritte.text: The property does not replace retirement provision. Neither care costs nor property tax can be paid out of a paid-off house.

schritte.text: Determine the outstanding balance at the end of the fixed-rate period and calculate the new instalment. Then check whether this instalment remains affordable and whether the loan will be paid off before the pension starts.
One earner receives only 60% of their net income for twelve months. The question to answer is how many monthly instalments are available as a liquid reserve.

schritte.titel: Check affordability for one partner alone
schritte.text: Check whether one of the two partners can carry the instalment alone, if necessary by letting part of the property. If that is not possible, the financing depends on the couple staying together.

bloecke.md: A reserve of six to twelve monthly instalments in the account costs return. However, it is the only protection against a loss of income leading to a forced sale. These costs can be quantified. Anyone who uses the money for a special repayment instead earns a risk-free and tax-free return equal to the borrowing rate, here 3.90%. An investment with fully taxable interest, such as an instant-access savings account, must yield 5.30% before tax to draw level. Capital income is subject to 25% flat-rate withholding tax (Abgeltungsteuer, Section 32d(1) EStG, Income Tax Act) plus a 5.5% solidarity surcharge (Section 4 SolzG 1995, Solidarity Surcharge Act), together 26.375%. The 5.30% therefore results from 3.90 divided by 0.73625. With 9% church tax, it is 5.42%. For an equity fund, 30% of the income is tax-free under the partial exemption (Teilfreistellung) in Section 20(1) InvStG (Investment Tax Act), so the threshold there is 4.78%. The saver's allowance (Sparer-Pauschbetrag) of €1,000 per person (Section 20(9) EStG) only lowers the threshold noticeably for small portfolios. Nevertheless, the reserve should not go into special repayments. Its purpose is to avoid a sale at the wrong time, and for that the return plays no role. For let properties, the deductibility of interest on debt changes this calculation.

## Statutory right of termination as an option

A longer fixed-rate period costs a premium. On 3 September 2026, according to Dr. Klein, offer rates for ten-year fixed-rate periods were at 3.97% effective, fifteen-year ones at 4.17%, twenty-year ones at 4.30% and thirty-year ones at 4.48%. The premium of around 0.3 points for ten additional years of certainty costs roughly €1,000 to €1,100 a year in the base case, so just over €10,000 over the first ten years.

This is offset by a one-sided right of the borrower. Under Section 489(1) no. 2 BGB, the borrower can terminate the loan ten years after receiving it in full, giving six months' notice, regardless of a longer fixed-rate period and without an early repayment charge. This right cannot be excluded by contract. A twenty-year fixed-rate period therefore only binds the borrower for ten years. For the following ten years, it secures the interest rate for the borrower without the borrower having to use this protection. The premium is the price of this option.

Whether the option is worthwhile is shown by comparing it with the potential damage. In the base case, follow-up financing at 5.90% instead of 3.90% for the same remaining term costs around €69,000 in additional interest, spread over the entire remaining term of just under 18 years. A twenty-year fixed-rate period only protects against this in years 11 to 20, and at its own interest rate of 4.30% instead of 3.97% effective. According to the same calculation, it avoids roughly €47,000 in additional interest. Measured against a premium of €10,000, that is a ratio that is open to debate, but that should feed into the decision.

mitnehmen: The fixed-rate period only secures the interest rate, and with a 2% initial repayment rate, just over three quarters of the loan is still outstanding after ten years.
A higher initial repayment rate is the most effective protection against interest rate risk, and the step from 2% to 3% has the strongest effect.
A stress test calculates with both stagnating and growing income, because the instalment is fixed by contract, but income growth is not.

Unemployment benefit I replaces around 60% of flat-rate net pay; with basic income support (Grundsicherungsgeld, formerly Bürgergeld), the interest on the debt for an owner-occupied home is covered, but not the repayment.
Section 489(1) no. 2 BGB turns every fixed-rate period of more than ten years into a one-sided option for the borrower, whose price is the interest rate premium.

begriffe.text: The risk that the outstanding balance remaining after the fixed-rate period has to be refinanced at a higher interest rate. It grows with the size of the outstanding balance and falls with a higher initial repayment rate and a longer fixed-rate period.

Annuity plus running costs (maintenance, property tax, insurance, non-recoverable service charge) in relation to net household income. It is more meaningful than the pure instalment ratio, because it includes the running costs of the property.

The ability, checked by the bank, to service interest and repayments from income on a lasting basis. It is the basis of the creditworthiness assessment required under Section 505a BGB and is calculated using flat-rate cost-of-living allowances, not the household's actual expenses.

Compensation for the interest loss that a bank suffers when a mortgage loan is repaid early. The cap in Section 502(3) BGB does not apply here; the amount depends on how the interest rate level has developed since the contract was concluded.

Under Section 421 BGB, each of several borrowers owes the full amount, and the creditor can demand it from each of them individually. Agreements on how it is divided apply only between the debtors (Section 426 BGB).
